column1: # COMMITTED ARTIFACT IDENTITY.  Added 2026-08-02 (adversarial review, run 10).
# INPUTS_SHA256 was PRINTED by both gates and COMPARED TO NOTHING, so no run
# could ever fail on identity drift: the line was a receipt for a human who was
# never asked to check it.  These are the expected values; the gates now fail if
# the computed hash differs.
# THIS FILE IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE HASHED SET.  The hash covers the 32 cone
# files plus cert-baseline*.tsv and cert-statements-*.tsv.  Section 35 of the
# claims log records the trap: the log is itself a cone input of both gates, so
# writing a receipt into it changes the value the receipt reports.  A pin stored
# inside the hashed set would have the same defect.
# Changing a cone file or a manifest REQUIRES updating this file in the same
# commit.  That is the point: re-baselining becomes a deliberate, reviewable act
# rather than a silent one.  Recompute with LC_ALL=C (the collation pin -- see
# section 35); host and container then agree by construction.
# RE-BASELINE LOG.  Every change to these values is deliberate and must say why.
#   fork 211d6194fd972716eaeee792bcd74531 -> 3949c473....  THREE COMMENT AND
#   RECEIPT CHANGES, NO PROOF CHANGE.  Both censuses were verified identical
#   across the re-baseline (split 975 keys / 1055 rows, added=0 removed=0;
#   fork 1009 / 1089, no delta), so the assumption set is untouched.
#     (a) cert_gate_split.sh now prints ECO_PURGED alongside ECO_REMAINING.
#         ECO_REMAINING=0 could not distinguish "nothing was stale" from "180
#         stale objects were removed", and run 22 began as the second case.
#     (b) scratch/tier0_degenerate_encoder_excluded.ec header corrected: it
#         asserted a discriminating power the run-14 review disproved.  The
#         control is retained and still MUST-FAIL for its declared reason;
#         only the header changed.
#     (c) C10DeployedGeometry.ec section 41 records (a), (b), and the fact that
#         a zero census delta says nothing about a DEFINED op such as pkfors_of.
#   Recomputed with LC_ALL=C on BOTH host and container; the split value agreed
#   in both, which is the section-35 collation pin still holding.
#   7ab20d2a....  THIS ONE CHANGES THE ASSUMPTION SET ON PURPOSE -- read it.
#     (a) cdrafts-split/FORS_C_TreePort.ec (1733 lines) ADMITTED TO THE SPLIT
#         CLOSURE.  It was in NEITHER closure, so nothing in it was
#         gate-enforced.  Split census 1055 -> 1155 rows (LEDGER 228->239,
#         PARAMETERS 169->217, BINDINGS 334->341, MEANING 324->358).  The
#         assumptions did not appear; they became VISIBLE.  Nine statements
#         pinned, EXPECT_PINS 66 -> 75.  The new ledger admit is
#         FORS_C_TreePort::extract_op (admit:3b102492d8ec) -- the OpenPRE branch,
#         blocked on an UPSTREAM interface change, now impossible to lose track of.
#     (b) BOTH gates: re-sort after `uniq -c` before `comm`.  `sort | uniq -c`
#         orders by KEY then prefixes a COUNT, so the result is not whole-line
#         sorted and `comm` -- which requires that -- warned on the live
#         baselines.  I could NOT construct a wrong added/removed count in three
#         attempts, so this is latent fragility, not a demonstrated defect; the
#         fix is verified answer-preserving (added=100 both ways).  Fixed because
#         a spurious sortedness warning on the census comparison would mask a
#         real one.  The FORK census itself is unchanged at 1089 rows.
# 2026-08-04 (run 24).  split 058ef102... -> e3625fdd....  Fork UNCHANGED
#   (7ab20d2a...): nothing in the fork's hashed set moved.
#   Option (a): the instrumented three-flag Gproc game EUF_CMA_Gproc_V, plus
#   gproc_V_eq / gproc_V_split / gproc_Q_decomposition.  Census +1 row, and it is
#   a MEANING row (module:fbc0ec28fb21), not a LEDGER row -- LEDGER STAYS AT 239,
#   so this commit adds three theorems and NO assumption.  EXPECT_PINS 75 -> 78.
#   IT DOES NOT BOUND Q.  gproc_Q_decomposition is an exact equality whose
#   decomposition step is probability algebra valid for ANY flags; its content is
#   that the flags are MM45's (FORS_ES.ec:3216-3242), making each of the three
#   terms a target for a known reduction.  Q = T1+T2+T3 with all three unreduced
#   is still compatible with Q = 1.
# 2026-08-04 (run 25).  split e3625fdd... -> b09d8a8d....  Fork UNCHANGED.
#   COMMENT-ONLY, retracting a false claim I put in the run-24 header: that the
#   keygen bricks are "INERT ... not a step the template ever takes".  The grep
#   fact (no consumers) and the CASCADE claim are true; the INFERENCE is false --
#   every branch REDUCTION opens with a keygen correspondence in its simulation
#   invariant (FORS_ES.ec:5951-5952 for TRCO, :4840-4841 for TRH), and the pk
#   pool it characterises is `pkfors_of` verbatim.  Census UNCHANGED at 1156 rows
#   (added=0 removed=0); only the identity moves, because the file is hashed.
# 2026-08-05 (run 26).  split b09d8a8d... -> 837da057....  Fork UNCHANGED.
#   cdrafts-split/GprocVI.ec ADMITTED TO THE CLOSURE -- the V->VI hop, ADMIT-FREE.
#   Census 1156 -> 1159, and all three added rows are MEANING (the module bodies
#   GprocTreeVI, GprocKgVI, EUF_CMA_Gproc_VI).  LEDGER IS UNCHANGED AT 239: nine
#   theorems entered the cone and not one new assumption.  EXPECT_PINS 78 -> 87.
#   This is a PREREQUISITE for T3 (MM45 proves its TRH/TRCO branches over _VI,
#   not _V), not a bound.  Q remains unbounded.
# 2026-08-08.  split 837da057... -> 091c5dbc...  Machinery-only re-baseline:
#   cert_gate_split.sh gains PHASE 1e, which runs `easycrypt cli` over the four
#   base targets and every closure file and requires ZERO ^<tty>: diagnostics.
#   Reason: the two drivers disagree.  `tws_uniq` (scratch/_uniq.ec) passed
#   `easycrypt compile` four times and failed under `cli` with "cannot prove
#   goal (strict)" on the byte-identical file -- two steps closing on smt luck,
#   one discharging three side conditions for `u` and failing on the
#   identically-shaped ones for `v`.  No other phase can see this: the file
#   compiles, the lemma is saved, the statement digest is unchanged, the census
#   shows no admit, and an admit sweep reports 0.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE CHANGED in this re-baseline -- the delta is the gate
#   script alone, which is inside the hashed set by design.
#   Phase behaviour verified on four cases before adoption: clean file OK;
#   incomplete proof FAIL with its diagnostic; bogus include FAIL; and
#   easycrypt-not-on-PATH FAIL via the per-command prompt floor -- that last is
#   the fail-open the floor exists for, since a run that never happens also
#   emits zero diagnostics.
#   Cost: roughly doubles PHASE 1's prover work (FORS_ES.ec alone ~7 min).
# 2026-08-08 (second).  split 091c5dbc... -> ee902c82395aa7fd83547627a66af55c.  Machinery-only again:
#   cert_gate_split.sh gains PHASE 1f, and cert-watched-split.tsv +
#   scratch/sweep.py join the hashed machinery set.
#   PHASE 1f gates scratch/_t1.ec, _t2.ec, _t3.ec -- the Q = T1 + T2 + T3
#   branch proofs -- which nothing gated before: T2 and T3 had been at admit=0
#   for weeks with no mechanism to notice a break, and the cli defect that
#   motivated PHASE 1e lived in exactly these files.  They are WATCHED, NOT
#   CERTIFIED: absent from the closure, required by nothing, no census row, and
#   T1 carries an admit by design.
#   The MANIFEST is hashed; the WATCHED SOURCES are not.  Hashing work in
#   progress would force a re-baseline on every edit, which trains the operator
#   to re-baseline without reading -- worse than not hashing them.  Their
#   integrity is asserted by exact counts plus statement digests instead.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE CHANGED.
# 2026-08-08 (third).  split ee902c82... -> 95756d06403aa6b0e752084db8d5750c.  CORRECTION, machinery only.
#   PHASE 1e now runs `easycrypt cli -iterate`.  The four failures the previous
#   entry recorded as an open question were NOT defects: `compile` iterates the
#   smt call by default and `cli` does not, so the phase was comparing two smt
#   regimes.  Diagnosed to a 41-line repro (compile OK / cli 1 diagnostic /
#   `cli -iterate` 0), after ruling out timeout, prover parallelism and theory
#   scoping BY MEASUREMENT.  All four files go to 0 diagnostics with -iterate.
#   The claim that tws_uniq had been "closing on smt luck" is withdrawn; its
#   grounding is kept because supplying a named fact beats relying on axiom
#   selection, but it fixed no defect and nothing was ever unsound.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE CHANGED.
#   cert-watched-split.tsv records _t1.ec at 2 admits (was 1), because
#   Eqv_OCMA_sign -- the oracle equivalence for the forge call -- is now stated
#   with its proof deferred, and its statement digest is pinned.
#   The 95756d06 run was GREEN (28 cli files, 0 disagreements; 3 watched, 0
#   failures), so this re-baseline moves off a verified receipt.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE CHANGED; no gate machinery changed.
# 2026-08-08 (fifth).  split 5e33c086... -> 9ed1c93a5477907a69a41ceeb577feb0.  MANIFEST ONLY:
#   _t1.ec 2 -> 3 admits.  Eqv_OCMA_sign's LOOP now typechecks and its `while`
#   applies -- the two sign loops align -- leaving the body and the entry/exit
#   admitted.  Statement digests unchanged (3d9e3a2e... etc).
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE, NO GATE MACHINERY CHANGED.
#   _t1.ec 3 -> 2 admits.  Eqv_OCMA_sign's LOOP BODY is discharged; only the
#   entry/exit remains.  Statement digests unchanged (3d9e3a2e... etc) -- the
#   proof added two bound conjuncts to the `while` invariant, which is
#   proof-internal, so pinning the statement while writing the proof worked as
#   intended.
#   Two must-fail controls RUN SERIALLY (the parallel-load lesson) and graded by
#   FAILURE REASON, not by exit status:
#     A  leaves-window index perturbed by +1  -> fails IN the hresult block,
#        "[by]: cannot close goals".
#     B  `tidx{2} < nr_trees 0` deleted from the invariant with the peel depth
#        HELD FIXED (replaced by `tidx{2} <= tidx{2}`, same conjunction shape,
#        so no intro pattern shifts) -> fails at the end of hchar, "cannot prove
#        goal (strict)".  B is the one that matters: it shows the added bound is
#        load-bearing rather than decoration.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE, NO GATE MACHINERY CHANGED.
# 2026-08-09 (second).  split 4d616074... -> 956c9acfd4ddd7398890f113855a4a28.  MANIFEST ONLY:
#   _t1.ec 2 -> 1 admit.  Eqv_OCMA_sign IS FULLY PROVED -- entry, body and
#   exit.  The single remaining admit is t1_opre_bound itself.  Statement
#   digests unchanged (3d9e3a2e... etc): the proof strengthened the `while`
#   invariant with the lidxs <-> os coverage relation, which is proof-internal.
#   WHY THE INVARIANT HAD TO GROW, since "prove the entry and exit" sounds like
#   it should not touch the body: a cli dump showed the exit obligation reads
#   `forall sig_L os_R sigFORSTW_R, ... => <post mentioning os_R>` while the
#   invariant never mentioned `os`.  That goal is not hard, it is UNPROVABLE --
#   its conclusion constrains a variable its hypotheses do not name.  So the
#   coverage relation moved into the invariant and all three parts were proved
#   against the new one.
#   Two must-fail controls, SERIAL, graded by FAILURE REASON:
#     C  invariant tail off by one (drop (n+1) for drop n) -> fails in the BODY
#        at the cov_step rewrite, "nothing to rewrite".
#     D  `idxs.`2 < k` deleted from the coverage ranges with the conjunction
#        shape HELD FIXED (becomes `idxs.`2 <= idxs.`2`) -> fails in the ENTRY
#        at flat_inj, "the given proof-term proves 0 <= idxs.`2 < k, it does
#        not apply to the goal".
#   C and D fail in DIFFERENT halves, which is the point: they show the body's
#   list bookkeeping and the entry's index inversion are each load-bearing, and
#   neither is closing for the other's reason.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE, NO GATE MACHINERY CHANGED.
# 2026-08-09 (third).  split 956c9acf... -> 5cb564d13db1f92b6d47313ec757a9ab.  MANIFEST ONLY:
#   Eqv_OCMA_sign's statement digest moves 3d9e3a2e -> b4fc971e, DELIBERATELY.
#   Its post now restates its pre conjunct for conjunct: `call (: I)` against an
#   abstract adversary needs `={arg} /\ I ==> ={res} /\ I`, and the first
#   version dropped the leavess and xs characterisations from the post, so
#   t1_opre_bound's forge call could not have used it.  Caught by trying to use
#   the lemma, not by review -- which is the argument for landing the consumer.
#   The sign call writes neither leavess, xs nor sks; the exit gained two
#   `exact`s.  Admit count unchanged at 1.
#   Between this and the previous entry, the heaviest smt step inside
#   t1_opre_bound was GROUNDED (83653f5) -- watched source, outside the hashed
#   set, so it moved no identity; it is what took the gate from RED to GREEN.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE, NO GATE MACHINERY CHANGED.
#   cert-watched-split.tsv records scratch/_t1.ec at 1 -> 0 admits, because
#   t1_opre_bound's win condition (T1-T5) is now DISCHARGED.  The T1 branch of
#   Q = T1 + T2 + T3 is admit-free, as T2 and T3 already were.
#   NO CERTIFIED SOURCE, NO GATE MACHINERY CHANGED.  The watched sources are
#   deliberately outside the hashed set (see the header of that manifest), so
#   the ~200 lines of new proof in scratch/_t1.ec move no identity by
#   themselves; what moves it is the recorded expectation about them, which is
#   exactly the property that makes the count an assertion rather than a note.
#   All three pinned statement digests are UNCHANGED -- 035f68ac / 1666e835 /
#   b4fc971e -- so nothing was proved by weakening what was claimed.
#   The new helper t1_win leans only on GprocVI, FxChain and GprocFORSC10, all
#   three IN closure-c10-split.txt and all three at admit=0 axiom=0 sorry=0
#   (checked, not assumed -- the file's own note about pkfromsig_cf is that
#   reaching for an uncertified lemma would pull it into the cone).
# 2026-08-10 (second).  split 6d3c200e... -> ed5ddead0a28bdc0f462af81e53c7ef7.
#   THE BIGGEST DELIBERATE MOVE THIS FILE HAS RECORDED: T1/T2/T3 ARE PROMOTED
#   INTO THE CERTIFIED CLOSURE, so this re-baseline covers CERTIFIED SOURCE and
#   GATE MACHINERY, not just a manifest.  Four things moved:
#   (1) closure-c10-split.txt 24 -> 28: GprocT1Opre, GprocT2Trh, GprocT3Trco
#       (VERBATIM copies of scratch/_t1,_t2,_t3.ec -- no proof edits) and the new
#       GprocQBound.ec, which composes them into `gproc_Q_bound`.
#   (2) cert-statements-split.tsv 87 -> 95 pins; EXPECT_PINS moved with it.  The
#       seven relocated digests are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the watched ones
#       is the check that relocation changed nothing but location.
#   (3) cert-baseline-split.tsv +16 census rows, ALL module:/operand:/
#       clone-discharge:.  ZERO new admit/axiom/declare-axiom rows -- promotion
#       grounds the Q bound without growing the assumption set.
#   (4) cert_gate_split.sh: the watched phase's `-ge 3` anti-truncation FLOOR
#       became the committed EXPECT_WATCHED=0.  A floor cannot say "deliberately
#       none left".  The replacement is strictly stronger (it also fires on an
#       unexpected addition) and was tested in isolation at 0/1/3 rows; the
#       integration case is honestly NOT covered -- see the note at the guard.
#   cert-watched-split.tsv keeps its header and history but has ZERO data rows:
#   the three files are covered by PHASE 1/1b/1c/1d/1e as closure TARGETS now,
#   which is strictly more than the watched phase gave them.
#   WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not discharge the capstone's H-TREE-MULTI
#   premise.  SphincsC10CapstoneWired.ec:566 carries exactly `gproc_Q_bound`'s
#   statement at R_fors_p(F), and its mtree_* reals ARE instantiable binders --
#   but F is not declared disjoint from 9 of the 11 modules the composition
#   needs, so it does not typecheck there.  Wiring it requires narrowing a
#   headline theorem's hypothesis and is left as a deliberate decision.
#   THE Q LEG IS WIRED INTO THE CAPSTONE.  New closure member GprocQWired.ec
#   (closure 28 -> 29, pins 95 -> 96, EXPECT_PINS with it).  Census delta ZERO --
#   the file declares one lemma and no module/op, so it adds no baseline row and
#   no assumption.
#   WHAT MOVED, IN CONTENT: EUFCMA_SPHINCS_PLUS_C10_GROUNDED discharges the
#   H-TREE-MULTI premise by instantiating the tree reals at Q ITSELF, so its RHS
#   carries Q = Pr[EUF_CMA_Gproc_I(R_fors_p(F)) : res /\ !covered] unreduced --
#   and that file says so in terms ("nothing here bounds it below 1, and if
#   Q = 1 this bound is as uninformative as the free-real version was").
#   EUFCMA_SPHINCS_PLUS_C10_QWIRED instantiates the SAME parametric capstone at
#   the three branch advantages instead, discharging the premise via
#   gproc_Q_bound -- by a REDUCTION rather than by reflexivity.  Q is replaced by
#   one SM_DT_OpenPRE and two SM_DT_TCR_C terms.
#   NOTHING IN SphincsC10CapstoneWired.ec IS EDITED: QWIRED derives from the
#   parametric lemma, so every pinned digest in that file is unmoved and the
#   GROUNDED lemma remains available beside it.
#   THE PRICE, STATED: F carries nine more separations, so QWIRED applies to
#   strictly fewer forgers than GROUNDED.  That narrowing is NECESSARY, not
#   decorative -- removing even one (-EUF_CMA_Gproc_V) makes the proof fail with
#   "the module R_fors_p(F) is not allowed to use the module(s) F".  And it does
#   NOT make the bound numerically meaningful: Pr[M.F.ITSRC10 ..] is still
#   carried unreduced and remains the honest headline term.
#   TWO CHANGES, both from the 2026-08-10 adversarial review (GPT-5.6 + Kimi K3,
#   run independently; they converged on the state being sound and diverged on
#   what to do next, which is where the value was).
#   (1) QWIRED ANTI-VACUITY, COMMITTED AND GATED.  EUFCMA_SPHINCS_PLUS_C10_QWIRED
#   adds NINE module separations to the forger F; every separation narrows the
#   theorem, and an unsatisfiable set would make it vacuous -- proved, gated,
#   GREEN, and about nothing.  Both reviewers judged the set inhabited and found
#   no F <-> R(F) circularity (EasyCrypt restrictions are negative, one-directional
#   accessibility constraints).  Both ALSO said an uncommitted argument has zero
#   certification value, which was fair: the witness existed only as an untracked
#   scratch probe.  It is now `WitnessF` + `qwired_at_witness` in GprocQWired.ec,
#   pinned (EXPECT_PINS 96 -> 97).  The witness is STATEFUL and calls its oracle
#   -- a stateless module satisfies any {-X} vacuously and would witness nothing.
#   The lemma states the REAL instantiated bound, not `true`, so the pin protects
#   something: weakening its RHS to 0%r makes the apply stop matching (checked).
#   Census +1 row, module: (MEANING), no ledger movement.
#   (2) PHASE 4 -- THE GRINDING MARGIN IS NOW RECOMPUTED, NOT QUOTED.
#   FORS_C10.ec:89-91 justifies the "black-box route is a dead end" verdict with
#   "~28.1 vs ~130.6 bits, ~102 lost" and says in the same breath that the script
#   is NOT in this checkout.  Both reviewers named that the weakest receipt in the
#   repo.  tools/forsc_grinding_margin.py is vendored BYTE-IDENTICAL from
#   PQSigner_OS, cert-margin-split.tsv pins seven figures, and PHASE 4 recomputes
#   and compares them every run; both new files join the hashed machinery set.
#   Controls run before commit, each failing for its own reason: corrupt a value
#   -> "committed X, computed Y"; drop a row -> truncation guard fires; change the
#   script's output format -> "NOT PARSED (format drift?)" rather than a silent
#   pass.
#   CORRECTED 2026-08-11 (same day, GPT-5.6 adversarial review): the line here
#   first said the phase "asserts the script's own 4 guardrail self-tests
#   actually ran".  THAT WAS FALSE -- and it was a false claim about a CONTROL,
#   which is the worst place for one.  The four `[guardrail N] .. : OK` lines are
#   the HAPPY PATH of a normal run; the script's real negative controls live
#   behind `--self-test` (forsc_grinding_margin.py:275) and the phase never
#   invoked them.  It does now, and requires exit 0, the PASS line, and all 3
#   controls present.  Two further controls were run on THAT check: making self-test exit 1
#   -> "a guardrail did NOT fire when it must"; deleting one control's line ->
#   "ran only 2/3 negative controls".  The first attempt at the second control
#   was itself VACUOUS (my pattern missed an f-string, so the file was unchanged
#   and it "passed"); it was diagnosed and redone rather than accepted.
#   RETRACTED 2026-08-11 (later the same day, GPT-5.6 adversarial review, second
#   pass; VERIFIED against source before retracting).  The sentence removed above
#   claimed that invoking `--self-test` means "a guardrail neutered to print OK
#   unconditionally is caught".  THAT IS FALSE.  `self_test()`
#   (forsc_grinding_margin.py:275) takes an EARLY, SEPARATE path: it recomputes
#   `ratio = p_forsc(1)/p_plain_fors(1)` and `T_LAST < T` ITSELF, and never
#   executes normal guardrails 1-3 at lines 342-378.  So replacing those three
#   guard blocks with unconditional `print(... : OK)` and no `failures.append`
#   would still pass (i) the happy-path 4/4 count, (ii) `--self-test`, and (iii)
#   all seven pinned numbers.  What `--self-test` DOES prove is that the
#   underlying arithmetic inverts when the removed tree is shrunk -- a real
#   control over the MODEL, not over the guard blocks.  The seven pinned values
#   and the happy-path count are what actually constrain those blocks, and they
#   constrain the NUMBERS, not the branch logic.
#   THIS IS THE THIRD FALSE CLAIM I HAVE MADE ABOUT PHASE 4's CONTROLS in one
#   day (first: "the 4 OK lines are self-tests"; second: a vacuous negative
#   control on the fix; third: this).  The pattern is asserting what a control
#   covers from what it was WRITTEN to cover, without reading the path it takes.
#   NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY -- owner decision 2026-08-11, doc-retraction only.
#   Making `--self-test` exercise guards 1-3 requires editing
#   tools/forsc_grinding_margin.py, which would BREAK the byte-identity with
#   PQSigner_OS asserted in cert-margin-split.tsv's header -- turning a "not
#   frozen" provenance gap into an actively false provenance claim.  The correct
#   fix is upstream-first (fix in PQSigner_OS, re-vendor, re-pin), which is a
#   two-repo change and is NOT done here.  The gap is left OPEN and NAMED.
#   RELATED, unfixed and named: the gate pins only the LOCAL copy of the script.
#   Byte-identity with PQSigner_OS is true at this revision (md5 verified both
#   ways) but is a present-tense fact, not an invariant -- no upstream commit or
#   blob is pinned.
#   THIS CERTIFIES NOTHING.  The figures are heuristic generic-adversary
#   estimates that no EasyCrypt result carries; 130.6 is a per-candidate WORK
#   FACTOR, not a security level, and the pinned adv_log2_qh128 = -2.6 row is the
#   honest reading at a large query budget.  A5-ITSR remains cited-tcb.
#   CORRECTION TO THE 2026-08-10 ENTRY ABOVE, which this file should not carry
#   uncorrected: that entry said the promotion's 16 rows were "ALL module:/
#   operand:/clone-discharge:" and concluded "ZERO new admit/axiom rows -- the
#   promotion grounds the Q bound without growing the assumption set".  The
#   admit/axiom half is true.  The conclusion as phrased is NOT: cert_gate_split.sh
#   :503 counts clone-discharge IN THE LEDGER, and the receipts show LEDGER
#   239 -> 240.  The row is EI_OPRE (GprocT1Opre.ec:284), a `proof *` clone of the
#   standard library's ExactIter with BOTH obligations realized `by trivial`, so
#   no axiom was installed and the substance survives -- but "the assumption set
#   did not grow" was the gate's own vocabulary used wrongly, and in this repo
#   that is the defect, not a nitpick.  Caught by Kimi K3, confirmed against the
#   receipts.
#   THE Q LEG REACHES THE DEPLOYED LEVEL -- by PARALLEL-AND-PROMOTE, not in place.
#   Adversarial review 2026-08-11 (GPT-5.6 + Kimi K3, independent) found that
#   EUFCMA_SPHINCS_PLUS_C10_QWIRED had NO CONSUMER: the deployed chain still
#   applied GROUNDED, so the shipped headline carried the unreduced Q that
#   gproc_Q_bound exists to replace.  Calling the deployed result "Q-wired" would
#   have been false.  The two reviewers AGREED on that and SPLIT on the fix, which
#   is where the value was: Kimi argued in-place (no consumers, no doc quotes);
#   GPT-5.6 argued that QWIRED is not a same-domain strengthening -- it NARROWS F
#   by nine separations AND replaces an exact Q with an upper bound that may be
#   larger -- so mutating a published name would hide both changes at once.
#   GPT-5.6's mechanism was taken, and it matches this repo's own precedent
#   (Tier 0 Step 2: "The older lemma stays -- it is not repaired, it is superseded
#   for quotation").
#   ADDED, all in GprocQWired.ec so the dependency runs FORWARD along closure
